subject: english
question:
**Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:**

The organized sellers with the ability to control their price-lines, or pass on any increase in cost to customers, **should be able to maintain or improve profit margin.**

options.text: should be able to maintain or improve profit margins
will be able to maintains or improve profit margin
will be able to maintain or improves profit margin
will be abled to maintain or improve profit margin

solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. should be able to maintain or improve profit margins .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is written in a formal and hypothetical context, describing a situation where organized sellers can manage their price-lines and pass on costs to customers.
 
• The highlighted part of the sentence needs to be grammatically correct, concise, and consistent with the tone of the sentence.
 
• Option 1 is correct because it uses proper subject-verb agreement and a plural form of "profit margins," which matches the plural subject "organized sellers."
 
• Other options fail due to grammatical errors or incorrect verb forms:
 
 
• Option 2: "maintains" is incorrect because it mismatches with the plural subject "sellers."
 
• Option 3: "improves" is incorrect for the same reason as Option 2.
 
• Option 4: "abled" is grammatically incorrect and not a valid word in this context.
 
 

Correct sentence: *The organized sellers with the ability to control their price-lines, or pass on any increase in cost to customers, should be able to maintain or improve profit margins*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement:** Ensure that the verb matches the subject in number and tense.
 
• **Clarity:** Use concise and correct phrases to maintain the professional tone of the sentence.
 
• **Common Errors:**
 
 
• Using singular verbs for plural subjects or vice versa.
 
• Incorrect word forms, such as "abled" instead of "able."
